header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (CloudScale CTO), Lina (CloudScale Platform), Ravi (CloudScale Product)
summary: POC scoping call to size reserved GPU capacity for a 2-week proof-of-concept, define autoscale/burst strategy, fallback policies, and benchmark plan. Customer wants 95th pct latency targets and cost estimate; agreed to run load tests mid-next week and share prompt set. Recommended starting reserved pool 2xA100 (or equivalent), allow burst to 6 during peaks, fallback to quantized model variant and hosted route for overflow.
topics: success criteria, workload sizing (QPS/concurrency), reserved GPUs, burst capacity, fallback policies, benchmarks, timeline and next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're here to scope the POC for CloudScale, specifically capacity and autoscale. quick intro round?
[00:12] Carlos: Carlos Mendes, CTO at CloudScale. we'll be validating latency and cost for our summarization endpoint.
[00:19] Lina: Lina Park, platform. i'll own infra integration and VPC connectivity.
[00:24] Ravi: Ravi Shah, product, success criteria owner.
[00:29] Maya: Maya Chen, SE, i'll run the bench and help size GPUs.
[00:32] Jordan: Great. quick agenda: define success criteria, share workload characteristics, propose reserved GPU sizing and burst strategy, fallback behavior, and agree on bench plan and timeline.
[01:05] Carlos: Our SLA target for the POC is 95th percentile latency under 250ms for 512-token summaries, and we really want to understand cost per 1k requests. throughput is spiky, typical baseline 10 QPS, spikes to 60 QPS during business hours for 10-15 minute bursts.
[01:30] Maya: got it. are the 512 tokens real end-to-end or truncation? like avg gen length?
[01:36] Ravi: avg output token is ~350, sometimes 600 for long docs. inputs vary but usually 50-150 tokens.
[01:45] Maya: ok so sequence length distribution center around 500-700 tokens worst case. that'll impact GPU memory and batch sizing.
[01:55] Jordan: what's traffic shape for the POC? are you planning synthetic, or real traffic mirrors?
[02:01] Carlos: we'll provide 72 hours of traces and a 1k prompt set representative. initial bench should use recorded traces replay so we hit realistic burstiness.
[02:12] Maya: excellent. for POC we recomend reserved capacity for predictability: start with 2 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to handle baseline and steady concurrency; allow burst to up to 6 GPUs via autoscale policy for peak.
[02:31] Lina: curious about how bursted GPUs are billed in Redwood dedicated - is it per-minute or hourly? and if they scale down quickly is there a minimum?
[02:41] Jordan: billing detail we'll include in the pricing doc, but typically reserved commits are monthly, burst hours are usage-based. there's often a short cooldown to avoid thrash, like a 5-10 minute minimum.
[02:53] Ravi: what about fallback if burst capacity isn't available? we can't have requests fail.
[02:58] Maya: we recommend a multi-tier fallback: first, fall back to a quantized model variant (8-bit quant) on same pool to preserve latency but reduce throughput pressure; second, route overflow to Redwood hosted endpoints (slightly higher latency but reliable); third, implement graceful degradation like shorter summaries.
[03:15] Carlos: will quantized model degrade quality much? we care about ROUGE and user-visible regression.
[03:21] Maya: small quality drop, usually <5% on our evals for this model class; we will run A/B during bench to measure reg. we'll also pin model versions for POC.
[03:34] Jordan: success criteria recap: 95p latency <250ms for 512-token target on baseline, cost-per-1k under target (customer to provide budget threshold), and no more than 2% error/failures during peak. agreed?
[03:51] Carlos: agreed, let's capture that.
[04:00] Maya: ok workload sizing specifics: customer expects 10 QPS baseline with concurrency ~20 active sessions, spikes up to 60 QPS, average request size input 100 tokens. for those numbers our sim suggests 2 GPUs reserved, with batch windows at 20-50ms and token-parallelism optimizations.
[04:23] Ravi: can you send the sim numbers and assumptions? we'd like to review offline.
[04:27] Maya: yes, i'll export the perf model and assumptions.
[04:30] Jordan: on the burst strategy: autoscaler threshold triggers at 70% GPU util sustained for 30s, spin up to 1 extra GPU at a time up to max 6, with a cooldown 5 minutes. also we recommend pre-warm warm pools for scheduled high-traffic windows.
[04:47] Lina: network egress - we have strict egress for PII. any routing to hosted endpoints will need to pass through our approved egress rules and we prefer routing through our VPC peering to keep traffic internal.
[04:58] Jordan: noted - we'll coordinate with your networking team. for Private deployments we can deploy in your VPC so traffic never leaves. for Dedicated we can keep it in a customer VPC as well.
[05:10] Carlos: security checks: we're SOC2 in progress, need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO/SAML.
[05:18] Maya: Redwood supports audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO. we'll attach security docs.
[05:24] Ravi: bench plan and timeline?
[05:27] Jordan: propose 2-week POC: kickoff and infra setup day 0-2, bench prep and data ingestion day 3-5, perf runs day 6-9 with 3 full replay runs, analysis day 10-12, final review and decision day 14.
[05:43] Carlos: that works. cost sensitivity - what's the expected burst cost vs reserved?
[05:49] Maya: rough ballpark: reserved 2xA100 commit ~ $Xk/month (we'll provide exact numbers). burst to 6 for short periods will add usage charges; estimate per-hour for each burst GPU at usage rate. we'll lay out a model: baseline cost + cost for 2 hours/day of typical bursts etc.
[06:05] Ravi: and fallback routing to hosted endpoints, is there an additional egress or data retention concern?
[06:12] Jordan: hosted path will have standard retention and processing policies; we can set the hosted path to not persist logs if needed. all details in security appendix.
[06:20] Maya: bench specifics: we will run three classes of tests: steady-state baseline, spike replay using your traces, and stress test to find degradation knee (ramp to 100 QPS). for each we capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, and cost per 1k.
[06:36] Carlos: we want the scripts so we can run them internally too.
[06:39] Maya: yes i'll share the loadgen repo and a runbook.
[06:43] Jordan: decision criteria: if we can meet p95 <250ms on baseline and cost per 1k within your budget we'll propose an initial reserved contract (monthly) + optional burst credits for 3 months.
[06:57] Ravi: conversation about model variants - can you run quantized LLaMA-like 13B and also a 7B for fallback?
[07:04] Maya: yes, for the POC we can run two model variants: primary (rw-13b or equivalent), quantized 13b, and smaller 7b as final fallback. we will measure quality deltas.
[07:18] Carlos: any infra limits for autoscale spike-up time? we can't have cold start > 30s ideally.
[07:24] Maya: startup times depend on image/container startup and model load. warm start from snapshot/cache can be 8-20s for our infra; full cold boot may be 45-90s. hence pre-warm for predictable windows.
[07:37] Lina: ok will share expected daily spike schedule so pre-warm can be scheduled.
[07:41] Jordan: notes on fallback policies: try quantized on same pool first, then host route; also prioritise requests by SLA tier - premium requests get precedence and won't be routed to hosted path unless all options exhausted.
[07:58] Ravi: how do we measure quality for fallback? we need an automated regression check.
[08:02] Maya: we'll run a prompt set and compute automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) and manual spot checks. if degradation > threshold (you set it, default 5%) then we'll avoid fallback for production. for POC we'll log metrics.
[08:18] Carlos: we also require RBAC for who can trigger scale policies or modify model pinning.
[08:24] Jordan: Redwood Console supports role-based controls and audit trail. we'll propose least-privilege roles for your team.
[08:31] Maya: any compliance gating that would block hosted fallback?
[08:34] Lina: yes, some customers must keep data on-prem. for those flows we'd prefer private deployment, but for the POC we can do hosted fallback if we obfuscate or strip PII.
[08:46] Jordan: understood. we'll add a PII-handling checklist to the runbook.
[08:52] Ravi: timeline recap?
[08:55] Jordan: kickoff this week, bench scripts by 11-07, bench runs 11-07 to 11-09, analysis by 11-12, final review 11-14.
[09:04] Carlos: that schedule is fine.
[09:06] Maya: risk areas: model quality delta on quantized, network egress rules, and autoscale spin-up latency. we'll explicitly test these.
[09:17] Ravi: ok for next steps please send pricing and the security docs.
[09:21] Jordan: will do. any other questions?
[09:26] Carlos: one more - do you support KV cache reuse across sessions to improve latency?
[09:30] Maya: yes we have prefix/KV caching, session pinning options; for repeated docs we can get big gains. we'll propose cache TTLs in the bench.
[09:42] Jordan: great. let's recap action items then close.
[09:47] Maya: recap: Maya to share loadgen and perf assumptions by 2025-11-07; Jordan to share pricing and contract sketch by 2025-11-06; CloudScale to provide sample prompts and traces by 2025-11-06; Lina to confirm VPC/KMS constraints by 2025-11-08.
[10:07] Carlos: thanks all, looking forward.
[10:10] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench. bye.
[52:00] (call end)

Notes: transcription contains minor recognition errors and some product names may be mis-spelled (rw-13b instead of Redwood-13B). references in call to reserved A100 are shorthand for GPU class equivalence.
